findings.title: Rejected devices are cached as successfully admitted
findings.body: TagDevice now propagates ErrDeviceLimitReached, but tagDeviceUI still populates localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the limit is reached, a new device's first request fails while its cache entry remains. Every subsequent request with that device ID returns nil from the cache check, so Anonymous.Authenticate grants access for the next 29 minutes despite the limit. Cache only successful admissions, and ensure concurrent requests cannot observe an admission before the store operation succeeds.

findings.title: Make the capacity check and device admission atomic
findings.body: CountDevices runs separately from the subsequent INSERT, with no transaction or locking that serializes admissions. If the count is one below the limit, two requests for different new device IDs can both observe available capacity and both insert successfully. This also occurs across Grafana replicas sharing a database. Those excess devices then remain eligible for updates even after the limit is reached. Serialize the count-and-admit operation across instances and add a concurrent-admission test.

findings.title: Requests without a device header bypass the configured limit
findings.body: Authentication now relies on TagDevice returning ErrDeviceLimitReached to enforce the limit, but TagDevice immediately returns nil when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent. Consequently, even with a full device quota, an anonymous caller can omit this client-controlled header and continue accessing protected APIs without being counted or rejected. Enforce admission on anonymous API requests even when the header is missing, while explicitly handling any bootstrap requests that cannot yet supply a device ID.
